brands.d: London fine-art publisher of postcards, greetings cards and scraps, founded by Raphael and Ernestine Tuck; merged into British Printing Corporation in 1959.
Detroit Photographic Company, renamed 1905, publisher of Photochrom-licensed 'Phostint' colour postcards; bankrupt 1924.
Firm founded by Orell Füssli as Photochrom Zürich to exploit Hans Jakob Schmid's Photochrom process.
Chicago postcard printer known for large-letter 'Greetings from' cards; closed 1978, archive now at the Newberry Library.
Dundee photographic publisher founded by James Valentine; later owned by Waddington and Hallmark, ceased 1994.
Holmfirth publisher founded by photographer James Bamforth, famous for comic seaside postcards from 1910.
Sevenoaks printer and postcard and calendar publisher founded by Joseph Salmon; stopped trading in 2017.
Vienna design workshop founded by Josef Hoffmann, Koloman Moser and Fritz Waerndorfer, making goods including postcards until 1932.
Eastman Kodak, the Rochester photographic company that popularised roll-film cameras and amateur printing.
Coventry weaver whose Jacquard-woven silk pictures became known as Stevengraphs.
